library_preparation_preflight.summary: 3 of 4 uncovered dynamic-access entries are flyway-core's optional pluggable logging backends (slf4j, log4j2, apache-commons), which are never pulled in by the generated scaffold. Decompiling flyway-core-10.15.0.jar confirms: these are declared <optional>true</optional> in its POM, and FeatureDetector/LogFactory only reflectively instantiate the matching LogCreator class when the corresponding API class is present on the classpath. The 4th uncovered entry (SHA2$SHA256 via JdbcUtils) has no SHA/MessageDigest reference anywhere in flyway-core's own bytecode and is reachable through the existing H2 dependency already in build.gradle — no extra setup evidence found for it.

flyway-core reflectively instantiates Log4j2LogCreator when org.apache.logging.log4j.Logger is reachable; optional dependency not pulled in by default. log4j-api alone (no log4j-core) is sufficient since LogManager falls back to its own internal SimpleLogger when no core binding is present.

library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: To drive all three LogCreator reflection entries in a single test run, explicitly select logger names rather than relying on 'auto' detection: configuration.loggers("slf4j", "log4j2", "apache-commons") on FluentConfiguration before calling migrate(). Decompiled LogFactory confirms these three exact string literals (note the hyphen in 'apache-commons') map directly via ClassUtils.instantiate(...) to the three LogCreator classes, bypassing FeatureDetector entirely. Auto-detection would only ever activate one framework (slf4j > log4j2 > apache-commons priority order) and, for slf4j specifically, additionally requires a full SLF4J binding (StaticLoggerBinder for 1.x or an SLF4JServiceProvider for 2.x) to be present — which the API-only jar above does not provide — so auto-detection would silently fail to cover slf4j even with slf4j-api on the classpath. No environment variable or system property is needed for the logging entries. For the remaining SHA2$SHA256/JdbcUtils entry, no concrete setup requirement was found; it is likely reachable by broadening the existing H2-backed test (e.g. a scenario that exercises connection retry/backoff or an additional migrate/baseline/clean operation) rather than via new setup.
risks: The exact pinned versions for the three logging dependencies are suggestions for consistency with existing repo usage (slf4j-api 1.7.36, log4j-api 2.25.2, commons-logging 1.1.1 all already appear elsewhere in tests/src); any reasonably current stable release of each should work since only the API class needs to be classloadable.

Coverage for the SHA2$SHA256/JdbcUtils entry remains unverified — it may turn out to need a specific Flyway feature (e.g. schema-history locking retry) that the generated test doesn't naturally exercise, in which case local Gradle/Native Image verification will surface it as still missing.
